subject: Change default lavaan parallel processing on every core of a cluster

messages.author: 87ad015a869f13c2
messages.subject: Change default lavaan parallel processing on every core of a cluster
parts:
Hi everyone,

I want to fit a Thurstonian IRT model to my ordinal data (pairwise compairsons of item triplets). As this is really time-consuming, I intend to execute the code on the cluster of my university. Unfortunately, there seems to be a default in lavaan() to use a parallelized execution on every available core of the cluster simultaneously. Because this approach blocks all the cores for other researchers of my lab and as it is not efficient because the data is copied on every core again, I want to change this default, but I don't know how!

In the lavaan() source code, I did not find anything about parallel execution, so I tried other approaches like... 

1. options(mc.cores = 8L)
2. fit <- parallel::mclapply(lavaan::lavaan(lavaan_model,
                     data = lavaan_data,
                     ordered = ordered,
                     auto.fix.first = FALSE,
                     auto.th = TRUE,
                     parameterization = "theta",
                     estimator = "ULSMV"),mc.cores=8L)
3. R_FUTURE_AVAILABLECORES_FALLBACK=8 (in the prompt before executing the R script)

But nothing worked out. I would be really happy, if there is any advice for my problem!

Thank you very much
Andra

messages.author: 87ad015a869f13c2
messages.subject: Re: Change default lavaan parallel processing on every core of a cluster
parts:
In addition: Just adding lavaan::lavaan(..., parallel = "no") as it might be the approach for lavaan::lavaanList(...  , parallel = "no"  ) was not successful, either.


In case, anyone is interested in the code, I provide it below:

# input model
TIRTmodelCovStartOrthFixOrthFix <- '
# factor loadings (lambda)
O.Int =~ start(1)  * L1   * i1i2   + start(1)  * L1   * i1i3   + start(1)  * L34   * i34i35   
A.Coo =~ start(-1) * L2n  * i1i2   + start(1)  * L2   * i2i3   + start(1)  * L4    * i4i5     + start(1)  * L4   * i4i6    
[...]
P160 == 1
'
# define the model as lavaan input model
lavaan_model <- TIRTmodelCovStartOrthFixOrthFix

# input data and bring them into the right form
load("triplets_long.RData")
lavaan_data <- make_sem_data(triplets_long)

# order of pairwise comparisons
ordered <- names(lavaan_data)

# fit lavaan model
fit <- lavaan::lavaan(lavaan_model,

data = lavaan_data,
                      ordered = ordered,
                      auto.fix.first = FALSE,
                      auto.th = TRUE,
                      parameterization = "theta",
                      estimator = "ULSMV")

# summary
lavaan::summary(fit,standardized=TRUE,fit.measures=TRUE)

# function TIRT fit by Buerkner
TIRTfit <- function(fit, data) {
  version <- utils::packageVersion("thurstonianIRT")
  structure(nlist(fit, data, version), class = "TIRTfit")
}

# fit TIRT model
fitTIRTCovStartOrthFixOrthFix <- TIRTfit(fit = fit, data = lavaan_data)

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Change default lavaan parallel processing on every core of a cluster
parts:
On 5/6/22 14:11, 'Andra Kämpfer' via lavaan wrote:
> Unfortunately, there seems to be a default in lavaan() to use a
> parallelized execution on every available core of the cluster
> simultaneously.

I don't think this is true. In fact, lavaan() has ZERO code for
parallelization, and just runs a single job on a single core. Only the
lavaanList() and bootstrapLavaan() function have explicit support for
parallelization.

Are you sure that lavaan() is 'distributing' itself to the multiple
cores? Do you use other packages?

Yves.
